title: Response Econ Decomposition - Sketchbook & Heuristics
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketchbook for a token-level cost + latency decomposition UI that helps surface where tokens (and token classes) drive spend and tail latency per invocation. Not a final spec — exploratory sketches, interaction heuristics, and prioritized backlog for a first prototype in Console.

Audience:
- Product PMs (console)
- UX designers
- Frontend engineers working on the insights surface
- Observability and infra SMEs (cost-attribution owners)

High-level goals:
- Make per-invocation and aggregated token-level cost visible and explorable with minimal clicks.
- Map cost to observable sources: model variant, sequence length, KV cache hit/miss, batch size, hardware class.
- Surface tail-latency contributors and correlated token patterns (e.g., long continuous prompts, rare tokens).
- Provide actionable optimization suggestions (batching, caching hints, model/quantize suggestions).

Assumptions (for prototype):
- We have per-token attribution data from the runtime (service events include token counts and timing buckets).
- Backend can produce: per-invocation token timeline, per-token cost estimates, cache hit/miss flag per request, and model variant metadata.
- Initial dataset sample size: 1k invocations over 24 hours for a selected route.

Key UX principles driving sketches:
- Incremental reveal: summary first, then drilldown to the token timeline.
- Align cost and latency views on the same horizontal axis so users can correlate spikes.
- Lightweight heuristics: show potential optimization suggestions inline (non-blocking).
- Fast filters: route, model, region, hardware, cache-hit, time range, token-type (prompt/system/user/assistant).

Primary surface: "Econ Decomposition" panel (left-to-right):
[HEADER] Route selector | time-range | model variant | hardware
[SUMMARY ROW]  Avg cost / invocation | median latency | p95 latency | total invocations | top contributing token-groups
[VIS 1 - Aggregate waterfall] Stacked bars over time: token-cost (prompt tokens, completion tokens, KV rehydration, cross-region transfer)
[VIS 2 - Latency overlay] Thin line overlay on same chart showing p50/p95 latency. Hover aligns a vertical scrub line.
[VIS 3 - Token timeline scrub] When a user clicks a bar -> open the invocation timeline: left: invocation metadata; right: horizontal token timeline where each token is a tiny block colored by token-class and shaded by per-token cost.
[DRILLDOWN MODAL] Invocation detail modal shows: full prompt/response (redacted by default), token-by-token time delta (ms), token cost, cache-hit flag, KV size, GPU used, batch size, and a simple heuristic badge: e.g., "KV miss heavy", "Long assistant segment", "Subword fragmentation".

Sketch notes (visual affordances):
- Token blocks should be narrow at 1:1 sequencing; allow zooming (2x/4x) to view token text on hover.
- Color palette: keep low-chroma colors for token classes; use stronger accents for heuristic badges and cost hotspots.
- Use micro tooltips showing exact numbers and link to a permalink to the invocation for SRE debugging.
- Streaming-friendly: when viewing a live stream of invocations, new bars append to the right and highlight transiently.

Interactions / Microflows:
- Flow A: Investigate p95 spike
  1) From route dashboard click the p95 cell -> panel auto-filters to spikes timeframe.
  2) Hover waterfall to find a tall stacked segment -> click -> open invocation modal.
  3) In modal, toggle "Show token text" to reveal tokens and search for specific tokens/phrases.
  4) Click "Suggest Optimizations" to get pre-canned suggestions (batch smaller, enable prefix caching, quantize to int8 for this workload).

- Flow B: Find high-cost token groups across time
  1) Use filter token-type = assistant and token-length > 512 to narrow.
  2) Group-by token-class and show aggregated unit-cost per 1k tokens.
  3) Export top-10 token n-grams for evaluation.

Heuristic rules (early list to implement in backend):
- If >40% tokens in completion are unique vs prompt and avg token latency > 20ms -> flag as "generation-heavy".
- If KV-cache hits < 60% and rehydration bytes > 1MB/invocation -> flag "KV rehydration".
- If batch size > 16 and average per-token latency > expected baseline -> flag "possible misbatch".
- If p95 latency >> median by factor > 4 and correlated with specific token prefixes -> flag "token-tail".

Optimization suggestion UI (in modal):
- Show 2–3 ranked suggestions with expected delta (e.g., "Enable prefix caching — estimated 18% cost reduction for similar invocations").
- Each suggestion has an "Apply" (for Dedicated/Private customers with autoset rules) and "Create SE ticket" button.

Data density and performance constraints:
- Do not render every token for very long responses by default; show a sampled/aggregated view with an option to expand.
- For routes with >10k invocations in range, default to aggregated rollups and require user to drill into a sampled subset for raw tokens.

Accessibility considerations:
- Colorblind-safe palettes and high-contrast option.
- Keyboard-first interaction for scrub and modal navigation.
- Tooltips must be available to screen readers as aria-labels on hoverable elements.

Proposed MVP wireframes (priority):
1) Aggregated waterfall + latency overlay with hover scrub (horizontal bar chart) — P0.
2) Invocation modal with token timeline sample and heuristic badges — P0.
3) Filters & quick-suggest optimization panel — P1.
4) Export top token n-grams and link to evaluation harness — P2.

Backlog (raw notes & estimates):
- Build aggregate waterfall component (frontend) — 5 dev days — P0.
- Backend endpoint for per-invocation token timeline + heuristics (prod team) — 6 dev days — P0.
- Token timeline component (zoom + hover) — 4 dev days — P0.
- Optimization suggestion engine (heuristic rule engine) — 8 dev days — P1.
- Permalinks & SRE debug view integration — 3 dev days — P1.
- Export/eval hook to Evals infra — 5 dev days — P2.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- What is the canonical per-token cost formula (include infra overhead or just model token compute)? Decision needed from finance/costing.
- How do we securely surface token text for PII-sensitive customers? Per-customer toggle + redaction policy?
- For Hosted tier do we show exact dollar values or normalized units to avoid legal/noise?
- Should suggestions be actionable in Console for Hosted plans or only provide guidance? Licensing/legal question.

Next steps (short timeline):
- Review with infra/serving runtime team (week 1) to confirm data availability.
- Quick sketch session with design to refine palette and token micro-interactions (week 1).
- Spike: backend endpoint prototype returning 200 sampled invocations (week 2).
- Frontend prototype of aggregated waterfall hooked to spike data (week 3).

Notes to self / rough UX ideas to capture later:
- Micro-annotations on token timeline to indicate cached tokens (thin border) vs rehydrated (glow).
- Ability to save "investigation views" as bookmarks for recurring triage.
- Combine with cost-anomaly detector to auto-pin interesting invocations to the top.

References and related work:
- See linked Confluence page for raw telemetry schema and a sketch of the backend events.
- Related console features: invocation-trace and cost-breakdown (we will reuse components where it makes sense).

Status: draft. This doc is intentionally lightweight and conversational; move to a more formal PRD once initial spike validates the data model.
